rationale: The day after the midterms, every US and Boston outlet leads with the outcome: Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate (top three clusters, 9-13 US outlets each). It is the single dominant national story and the logical sequel to yesterday's Election Day entry. Speaker Mike Johnson's decision not to stay on as Republican leader is part of the same story (the House changing hands) and is noted in the caption, not drawn as a separate scene. Maine's Jackson-over-Collins result (New England) and the ballot-measure takeaways are left out of the picture to keep one clear image of Congress changing hands. The still-uncalled Mississippi Senate race is not claimed.

stories.name: Democrats win control of the House and Senate
facts: On Nov. 4, the day after the 2026 midterm elections, CBS News projected that Democrats had won majorities in both the House and the Senate; NBC News also reported Democrats taking both chambers.
Republican Sen. Ted Cruz said on his podcast, "We've lost the House, we've lost the Senate."
House Speaker Mike Johnson told his staff Wednesday morning he will not stay on as Republican leader in the new Congress; Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan announced bids for minority leader.

Hakeem Jeffries announced his candidacy for speaker in a letter to House Democrats; Democratic leaders laid out priorities including lowering costs, restoring ACA subsidies, reversing Medicaid cuts, undoing tariffs and ending the Iran war.
The new Congress begins in January; Mississippi's Senate race was still too close to call that evening.
stories.visual_notes: The US Capitol's east front (cast-iron dome with Statue of Freedom, colonnaded drum, central portico, Senate wing to the north and House wing to the south) seen from a low angle at the foot of the plaza at dawn the morning after. A huge stylized blue wave curls up behind and over the dome as an obviously symbolic backdrop for the widely used 'blue wave' phrase (PBS, CNBC, Cruz). Small generic figures in the foreground (a TV camera operator and a reporter, a few passers-by) are illustrative, not a specific reported event. No faces of real people, no text, flags with invented details, signs, numbers or seat counts.
stories.confidence: high: CBS News (House and Senate live pages, full read) and NBC News (Johnson article, full read; Nightly News headline) independently report Democratic control of both chambers; WCVB (full read) and the NYT headline corroborate. Johnson stepping aside is in NBC (full read) plus Axios, NPR and The Guardian headlines.
